title.narrative: Promoting Agroecology Practices for Biodiversity Conservation and Food security in the UNESCO Designated Mount. Elgor Transboundary Biosphere Reserves

description.narrative:
Agroecology, a holistic approach to food security, economic empowerment, and gender equality, as well as social inclusion, offers significant potential for promoting biodiversity conservation within UNESCO-designated Biosphere Reserves in East Africa. These reserves are vital ecosystems characterized by rich biodiversity and cultural significance, serving as important sites for promoting biodiversity conservation, sustainable development, scientific research, education, and cultural preservation. They contribute to global efforts to protect the planet's natural heritage and ensure a sustainable future for generations to come.
However, within the transition zone of the Biosphere Reserves, unsustainable agricultural practices threaten the delicate balance of these ecosystems, necessitating the adoption of agroecological approaches to ensure long-term environmental sustainability and food security. Thus, promoting agroecology practices for biodiversity conservation in UNESCO-designated Biosphere Reserves in East Africa presents a unique opportunity to address environmental challenges while improving food security and livelihoods for local communities. Our idea encompasses a comprehensive strategy to promote agroecology practices for biodiversity conservation in East African UNESCO Biosphere Reserves through the following activities:
a) Conducting a baseline assessment to identify existing agricultural practices, biodiversity hotspots, and potential threats within the three Biosphere Reserves in Kenya, Mauritius, Rwanda, and Tanzania. b) Identifying and disseminating tailored and gender-transformative agroecology training programs and educational materials for farmers and community members living in the transition zone of biosphere reserves. c) Promoting the adoption of agroecological practices among farmers and communities within UNESCO Biosphere Reserves in East Africa, thus enhancing biodiversity conservation. d) Developing knowledge products, including case studies, success stories, and policy briefs, to document and share promising agroecology practices for biodiversity conservation in eastern Africa. e) Fostering partnerships and collaboration among relevant stakeholders, including government agencies, NGOs, local communities, and academic institutions, to promote agroecological practices among communities, especially women, indigenous people, and youth.
The expected outcomes of this initiative include enhanced biodiversity conservation and ecosystem resilience within the Biosphere Reserves, improved soil health, water quality, and ecosystem services, strengthened capacity of local farmers, especially women and youth, and stakeholders in agroecology principles and practices, and enhanced collaboration and partnerships among relevant stakeholders for sustainable agriculture and biodiversity conservation within UNESCO Biosphere Reserves.
The adoption of agroecology practices will contribute to the long-term sustainability and conservation of biodiversity and ecosystem health within UNESCO Biosphere Reserves in East Africa.
